title: Guide - Peace in the Psalms - The Lord is my shepherd

parts.style: warm, gentle welcome, steady and unhurried
parts.text: Welcome to Peace in the Psalms. <short pause> This reading is called The Lord Is My Shepherd. <short pause> We'll listen slowly to Psalm twenty-three, spend a little while with it, and then pray. <short pause> You don't need to study anything. <short pause> You can simply listen.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: Let yourself be comfortable. <short pause> Set down whatever was in your hands. <short pause> If your mind is moving quickly, there's no need to catch it. <short pause> Just give it something gentle to walk beside... <short pause> one old song, one line at a time.

parts.style: gentle, a soft smile in the voice, illustrating
parts.text: A restless mind is often a counting mind. <short pause> It counts what is missing, and what might run out. <short pause> Not enough time. Not enough money. <short pause> Not enough of me to go around. <short pause> Listen for how this psalm answers all that counting, in its very first line.

The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want. <short pause> He maketh me to lie down in green pastures: he leadeth me beside the still waters. <short pause> He restoreth my soul: he leadeth me in the paths of righteousness for his name’s sake.
Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me; thy rod and thy staff they comfort me.

Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies: thou anointest my head with oil; my cup runneth over. <short pause> Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life: and I will dwell in the house of the Lord for ever.

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: I shall not want. <short pause> It doesn't say I will never feel need. <short pause> There is hunger in this psalm, and there are shadows, and enemies. <short pause> But there is no moment in it without a shepherd. <short pause> I shall not want... <short pause> because I am not the one who has to provide it all.

And notice how soon the psalm lets us lie down. <short pause> It comes near the beginning, before the valley has been crossed, before the table is set. <short pause> Rest isn't the prize at the end of this journey. <short pause> It is one of the first things the Shepherd gives.

So what has your mind been counting? <short pause> What are you afraid there will not be enough of? <short pause> Name it to yourself, without any shame. <short pause> And then set the first line right beside it. <short pause> The Lord is my shepherd... <short pause> even here. I shall not want.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: Let a few of the words rest on you now. <short pause> Green pastures... <short pause> and let your shoulders lower. <short pause> Still waters... <short pause> and let your breath slow. <short pause> He restoreth my soul... <short pause> and let yourself be someone who is being restored, rather than someone who must repair everything.

If green pastures feel very far from where you are, hold on to the middle of the psalm. <short pause> For thou art with me. <short pause> Those five words do not need good weather. <short pause> They are as true in the valley as they are beside the water.

Let's pray. <short pause> Lord, my Shepherd, <short pause> You know what I lack, and what I only fear I will lack. <short pause> Quiet the counting in me. <short pause> Lead me to the rest You have already made, and walk close when the path grows dark. <short pause> Let goodness and mercy find me today. <short pause> Amen.
Take the first line with you. <short pause> When the counting begins again, you can answer it softly... <short pause> the Lord is my shepherd. I shall not want. <short pause> Go gently, and be led.
